issues.description: Method renamed but inheritance contract silently changed without restating the spec
issues.detail: Wallet.sign_message was an implicit shared operation across Wallet, DIDWallet, NFTWallet with consistent signature (message, mode) -> (G1Element, G2Element). The replacement current_p2_puzzle_hash() has different signatures per subclass (NFTWallet takes an NFTCoinInfo arg, DIDWallet takes none) and no shared protocol declares it. SPEC-MISSING: there is no stated contract that p2_puzzle_hash is the substitutable abstraction.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic placed on base Wallet but called via main_wallet for unrelated DIDs/NFTs
issues.detail: Callers in wallet_rpc_api.py reach through self.service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic to derive keys for DID/NFT wallets. The transformation has nothing to do with main_wallet identity; placing it on Wallet conflates a pure synthetic-key derivation with wallet state. WRONG-BOUNDARY: this belongs as a free function in chia/wallet/util/signing.py alongside sign_message.

issues.description: verify_signature contract leaks RPC response type into the util layer
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types and returns it directly. The signing utility's contract should be (mode, key, message, signature[, address]) -> bool plus an error reason, not an RPC-shaped DTO. LEAKY-ABSTRACTION: the util module is now coupled to the request types module's evolution and cannot be reused without dragging RPC schema along.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum decision logic duplicated and lacks an explicit truth table
issues.detail: The free function signing_mode_enum derives a SigningMode from (is_hex, safe_mode) with an implicit fall-through to CHIP_0002 for the (False,True) case. The contract is not written down; a future fifth flag combination would silently land in the default. State the precondition/postcondition table at the function or, better, make it total via a match with an explicit branch.

issues.description: Module name util/signing.py is broader than the contract it actually fulfills
issues.detail: The module is specifically about CHIP-0002/BLS message signing and verification of human-facing messages, not general transaction signing (signer_protocol.py owns that). The name will attract unrelated additions and erode the boundary. Rename to util/message_signing.py to make the abstract data type explicit.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is a stale stub referring to a non-existent `request` parameter
issues.detail: The new function signature takes signing_mode/public_key/message/signature/address as keyword args, but the docstring still says ':param request:' carried over from the RPC method. The spec for the new contract has not been written; this is a small but telling SPEC-MISSING marker for a freshly extracted library function.

review.summary: The extraction creates a reusable signing utility, which is the right direction, but the contracts are under-specified. The shared method sign_message that used to act as an implicit cross-wallet protocol has been replaced by current_p2_puzzle_hash with inconsistent signatures across DIDWallet and NFTWallet and no declared protocol, so substitutability is now informal. convert_secret_key_to_synthetic on the base Wallet, then invoked via main_wallet for unrelated DID/NFT keys, is a wrong-boundary placement. The util module also leaks the RPC response type VerifySignatureResponse, weakening the abstraction. Tightening these contracts and moving synthetic-key derivation into the new util would make the boundary clean.
